heading: INT. HAND CAR WASH - BAY 2 - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HAND CAR WASH - BAY 2 - NIGHT
A concrete tunnel hosed down for the night.
Squeegees on hooks, foam drying on the walls, a radio playing low cumbia.
A black sedan is parked in the middle, suds still sliding off its hood.
VICTOR "VIC" ALMEIDA (40s, rubber apron, tattoo of a swallow on his neck) wrings out a chamois.
LORETTA SPENCE (50s, owner, reading glasses, bank bag on her hip) counts bills on an upturned bucket.
PAULIE OKAFOR-REYES (20s, new kid, headphones around his neck) dries the rims one at a time.
Loretta, you want me to lock the front?
units.name: VIC

units.text: In a minute.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Boss, is this guy coming back for his car?
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: Mind your rims.
units.name: VIC

units.text: He left it two hours ago. He said ten minutes.
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: Paulie, count the tip jar for me.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: There's only eleven bucks.
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: That's eleven more than the last time.
units.name: VIC

units.text: Loretta looks up, smiling, folds the bills into the bag, snaps it shut.
Paulie opens the trunk to wipe the seals.

Vic hangs a squeegee on its hook and crosses to the door and drops the latch; Loretta watches him do it and laughs lightly at a joke only she remembers; Paulie freezes with a rag in one hand and stares into the trunk.
Vic.
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: What?
units.name: VIC

units.text: Vic, there's a guy in here.
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: Loretta stops laughing.
Vic walks back, slow.
The three of them look down into the dark trunk.
Inside, a MAN in a suit lies on his side, eyes open, a neat hole in his collar.
Close it.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: He's dead. Boss, he's dead.
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: Paulie. Close it.
units.name: VIC

units.text: Vic, you said Dominguez would pick it up in the morning.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: That's what he told me.
units.name: VIC

units.text: Then why is it in my bay?
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Whose guy is that?
units.name: PAULIE

units.text: Nobody's.
units.name: LORETTA

units.text: Headlights sweep the front window.
A car idles outside.
The radio plays on.
Loretta lays the bank bag on the bucket, wipes her hands on her slacks, and turns to face the door.
